bloques.titulo: The double infinitive in Konjunktiv II past
texto: When a modal verb (**können, müssen, sollen, dürfen, wollen**) is used in Konjunktiv II past next to another verb in infinitive, the modal participle is not used, but its own infinitive: it is the phenomenon of **doble infinitivo** (**Ersatzinfinitiv**):
**Er hätte uns anrufen können** (He could have called us / could have called us).
**Du hättest den Chef informieren müssen** (You should have informed the boss / you would have had to inform the boss).
In main sentences, «hätte» goes in second position and the two infinitive ones are placed at the end (first the lexical verb, last the modal: **anrufen können**).
In subordinate sentences with **dass** or **weil**, the «hätte» auxiliary is immediately advanced in front of the double infinitive block: **...weil er uns hätte anrufen können**.

filas: I would have had / should have...
I would have had permission to...

frases.de: Der Kunde hat sich beschwert, weil die Lieferung zwei Tage zu spät ankam.
frases.es: El cliente se ha quejado porque la entrega llegó dos días tarde.
frases.en: The client complained that the delivery was two days late.
analisis: weil die Lieferung zwei Tage zu spät ankam
because the delivery was two days late

frases.de: Das verstehe ich. Du hättest mich sofort informieren müssen, als das Problem auftrat.
frases.es: Lo entiendo. Deberías haberme informado de inmediato cuando surgió el problema.
frases.en: I get it. You should have informed me right away when the problem came up.
analisis: Du hättest mich sofort informieren müssen
You should have informed me right away.

frases.de: Es tut mir leid. Ich dachte, ich hätte den Fehler allein beheben können.
frases.es: Lo siento. Creí que habría podido solucionar el error yo solo.
frases.en: I'm sorry. I thought I could have solved the mistake by myself.
analisis: ich hätte den Fehler allein beheben können
I could have solved the mistake myself.

frases.de: Beim nächsten Mal machen wir das gemeinsam. Wir hätten viel Zeit sparen können!
frases.es: La próxima vez lo haremos juntos. ¡Habríamos podido ahorrar mucho tiempo!
frases.en: Next time we'll do it together. We could have saved a lot of time!
analisis: Wir hätten viel Zeit sparen können
We could have saved a lot of time.

bloques.pregunta: What structure does the Konjunktiv II past adopt of a modal verb accompanied by another verb?

opciones.texto: The «hätte» Auxiliary with a double infinitive at the end of the sentence
opciones.explicacion: For example: «hätte anrufen können», «hätte prüfen müssen».

opciones.texto: The «wäre» auxiliary next to the modal participle
opciones.explicacion: The modal verbs always use «hätte» and require the infinitive replacement.

opciones.texto: The simple Präteritum form of the modal without auxiliary
opciones.explicacion: That form would express real past of indicative («konnte», «musste»), not unreal hypothesis.

bloques.pregunta: What does the phrase: «Du hättest die Unterlagen rechtzeitig einreichen müssen» mean?

opciones.texto: You should have delivered the documentation in time (and you didn't)
opciones.explicacion: It expresses a past obligation not fulfilled in the form of a constructive reproach.

opciones.texto: You'll have to file the papers next week.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase does not refer to a future obligation, but to a past period.

opciones.texto: You had permission to deliver the documents when you wanted.
opciones.explicacion: «Müssen» expresses need or obligation, not permission (which would be «dürfen»).

bloques.frase: Er ___ uns gestern Bescheid sagen können.

opciones.explicacion: With the double infinitive («Bescheid sagen können») the conjugated auxiliary is «hätte».
Masses never use «sein» as an auxiliary in composite times.
«hat» would indicate Perfekt of indication, not Konjunktiv II unreal.

bloques.frase: Ihr ___ den Fehler sofort melden müssen!

opciones.explicacion: With the pronoun «ihr» the correct form of Konjunktiv II of «haben» is «hättet».
It is indicative Präteritum in the real past.

bloques.frase: Wir hätten das Projekt früher abschließen können.

opciones.texto: We would have been able to complete the project sooner.
opciones.explicacion: It expresses a past possibility that did not materialize («hätten abschließen können»).

opciones.texto: We will complete the project with full certainty before the deadline.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase does not speak of future plans, but of a missed past opportunity.

opciones.texto: We couldn't work on the project because we didn't have permission.
opciones.explicacion: «Können» indicates capacity or possibility, not lack of permission.
In the double infinitive construction, «sollen» remains in its infinitive form («beachten sollen»).
The regular weak participle «gesollt» is necessarily replaced by the substitute infinitive.
«sollte» is the simple form, incompatible with the «hätte» auxiliary.

bloques.frase: Wir hätten das Projekt früher beenden können
bloques.traduccion: We would have been able to finish the project earlier.
bloques.explicacion: hätte + object + lexic infinitive + modal infinitive.

intro: To express what someone «habría podido» or «I should have done» in the past, the German combines «hätte» with a double infinitive structure (Ersatzinfinitiv).
